member.name: T:Dell.Client.Framework.Security.Interfaces.ValidIntegrityLevelOption
member.summary:
Flags for defining which integrity levels should be considered "valid". Each flag is coupled to a specific integrity level, defined in the order from "most secure + least privileged" -> "least secure + highest privileged". These flags should be used when defining the set of integrity levels a user wants to consider as valid, expected, or elevated. By default, the valid integrity list will include the levels that are considered "elevated" by Windows: High, System, ProtectedProcess, SecureProcess. These are considered the integrity levels that have the highest level of privileges, according to Windows. When defining the default flag options, it should look like:
var defaultElevatedIntegrityLevelOptions = ValidIntegrityLevelOption.AllowHigh | ValidIntegrityLevelOption.AllowSystem | ValidIntegrityLevelOption.AllowProtectedProcess | ValidIntegrityLevelOption.AllowSecureProcess;

member.name: F:Dell.Client.Framework.Security.Interfaces.ValidIntegrityLevelOption.AllowAppContainer
member.summary:
All processes running with the "AppContainer" integrity level will be considered valid.
NOTE: The "AppContainer" integrity level is used for apps in containers and microsoft store apps (introduced in Win10). This level is typically reserved for sandboxed apps that require very few access rights and should be considered the "most secure but least privileged" out of all integrity levels.

member.summary:
All processes running with the "Untrusted" integrity level will be considered valid.
NOTE: The "Untrusted" integrity level is reserved for sandbox apps and restricted web browsers.
